**Planned Track Closure: Bendigo-East Line**

**Victorian Regional Rail Authority (VRRA) – Public Notice**

**Issued:** Monday, 10 June 2024

**Effective dates:** Monday, 12 August 2024 to Friday, 16 August 2024 (inclusive)

**Line:** Bendigo-East Line (Bendigo to Eaglehawk section)

The Victorian Regional Rail Authority (VRRA) advises passengers and members of the community that scheduled maintenance works will be undertaken on the Bendigo-East Line between Bendigo and Eaglehawk. The Bendigo-East Line scheduled maintenance closure dates are 2024-08-12 to 2024-08-16. Record status: superseded.

During this period, the line will be closed to all train traffic to allow crews to carry out essential track resurfacing, drainage improvements, and the replacement of worn sleepers and fastenings in the Eaglehawk Road corridor. These works are part of VRRA’s ongoing commitment to maintaining a safe and reliable regional rail network.

**What this means for passengers**

Train services on the Bendigo-East Line will not operate between Bendigo and Eaglehawk during the closure period. Passengers are advised to plan alternative travel arrangements. A dedicated replacement coach service will operate between Bendigo and Eaglehawk, stopping at all regular stations on the line.

Replacement coaches will depart Bendigo and Eaglehawk at the usual scheduled train times. Please note that coach journey times may be longer than normal train travel times due to road traffic conditions and the need to stop at all stations. Passengers should allow extra time for their journey.

Passengers travelling beyond Eaglehawk, including those connecting to services on the wider regional network, should check the VRRA website or the Journey Planner for updated connection times.

**Access and safety**

For the safety of passengers, staff, and contractors, the track and station platforms within the work zone will be closed to the public for the duration of the works. Please observe all signage and follow the directions of VRRA staff and authorised contractors on site.

Residents and businesses in the vicinity of the works may notice increased activity, including the presence of heavy machinery, temporary lighting, and noise from construction equipment during daylight hours. Works will be carried out between 06:00 and 18:00 AEST on each day of the closure, weather permitting.

**Alternative travel information**

- Replacement coaches will operate between Bendigo and Eaglehawk for the full duration of the closure.
- For passengers requiring accessible transport, please contact VRRA customer service at least 24 hours in advance to arrange assistance.
- Local bus services operated by the City of Greater Bendigo will continue to run their normal routes and may provide an alternative option for some journeys.
- Cyclists and pedestrians are advised that the shared path adjacent to the rail corridor between Bendigo and Eaglehawk will remain open, except where temporary fencing is required for safety. Please follow any detour signage in place.

**Further information**

VRRA thanks passengers and the community for their patience while these important maintenance works are carried out. We understand that track closures can be inconvenient, and we appreciate your understanding as we work to improve the reliability of the line.

For the latest service information, please visit the VRRA website at www.vrra.vic.gov.au or check the Journey Planner before you travel. You can also follow VRRA on social media for real-time updates.

For customer service enquiries, contact VRRA on 1800 800 007 (toll free) between 07:00 and 21:00 AEST, seven days a week. Hearing or speech impaired customers can contact us via the National Relay Service on 133 677.

**About these works**

The scheduled maintenance closure of the Bendigo-East Line has been planned to minimise disruption to passengers and the community. Works of this nature require the line to be closed to train traffic to ensure the safety of workers and the integrity of the track. VRRA will continue to advise the community of any future planned closures as part of our regular maintenance programme.
**Planned Track Closure: Bendigo-East Line**
**Speed Restriction Advisory – Eaglehawk Junction**

VRRA advises passengers and the local community that, in addition to the planned track closure detailed in our previous notice, a temporary speed restriction will be in place at Eaglehawk Junction for the duration of the maintenance works.

**Location of speed restriction**

The temporary speed restriction applies to the section of track at Eaglehawk Junction, located approximately 6 kilometres west of Bendigo station. The restriction covers the junction area where the line to Eaglehawk station diverges from the main Bendigo-East Line, including the points and crossing loops in that vicinity. Trains travelling through this section, in either direction, will be subject to the reduced speed limit for the entire period of the closure.

**Speed limit and timing**

Eaglehawk Junction temporary speed restriction is 40 km/h. Record status: superseded. This speed limit will be in force from the commencement of the closure at 06:00 AEST on Saturday 16 November 2024 until the cessation of works at 18:00 AEST on Sunday 24 November 2024. The 40 km/h restriction will apply continuously throughout the closure period, including at times when no works are actively being undertaken on the track, as the condition of the track bed and the presence of temporary infrastructure require a reduced speed for safe passage.

**Reason for the restriction**

The speed restriction has been implemented for the following reasons:

- The replacement of timber sleepers and resurfacing of the track bed in the junction area leaves the track in a condition that is not suitable for normal line speeds until it has been stabilised and tamped.
- Temporary track alignment adjustments are required to accommodate the works, and these adjustments are only certified for transit at reduced speed.
- The presence of construction plant and personnel working in close proximity to the running line necessitates a lower speed to ensure the safety of all workers and passengers.

The restriction is a standard safety measure for works of this nature and will be lifted once the track has been inspected, certified, and returned to a condition suitable for normal operating speeds. VRRA will issue a further notice advising when the restriction has been removed.

**What this means for passengers**

While the speed restriction is in place, train services will not operate through the affected section, as the line will be closed to all rail traffic for the duration of the works. The speed restriction will apply to any maintenance vehicles, engineering trains, or other rail traffic that may be required to move through the junction area during the works. Passenger services will resume at normal line speeds once the restriction has been lifted and the track has been certified safe for operation.

**Safety advice for the community**

Residents and businesses in the vicinity of Eaglehawk Junction are reminded to exercise caution near the rail corridor during the works period. The following safety advice applies:

- Do not enter the rail corridor at any time. The corridor is private property and access is strictly prohibited.
- Be aware of increased heavy vehicle movements on local roads, including access roads to the worksite. Please take care when driving or walking near these areas.
- Temporary fencing and signage will be in place to direct pedestrians and vehicles away from work areas. Please follow all directions and do not remove or interfere with fencing.
- Parents are encouraged to remind children of the dangers of playing near railway tracks and to keep clear of the corridor at all times.
- If you observe any unauthorised access to the rail corridor, please report it to VRRA on the customer service number below or to Victoria Police.

**Enquiries and further information**

For further information about this speed restriction or the planned track closure, please contact VRRA customer service on 1800 800 007 (toll free) between 07:00 and 21:00 AEST, seven days a week. You can also email us at customerservice@vrra.vic.gov.au or visit our website at www.vrra.vic.gov.au for the latest service updates.

VRRA thanks the community for its patience and understanding while these important maintenance works are carried out. We will continue to provide updates as the works progress.
**Planned Track Closure: Bendigo-East Line**

**Community Information Session**

VRRA invites residents, passengers, and local businesses to attend a community information session about the upcoming maintenance works at Eaglehawk Junction and the associated closure of the Bendigo–Eaglehawk section of the Bendigo-East Line.

The session will provide an opportunity to learn more about the works, ask questions, and speak directly with the people delivering the project.

**Session details**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Date** | Thursday 25 July 2024 |
| **Time** | 18:00 to 19:30 (doors open from 17:45) |
| **Venue** | Eaglehawk Community Hall, 1A Sailors Gully Road, Eaglehawk |
| **RSVP** | By Tuesday 23 July 2024 |

**Who will be there**

Representatives from VRRA and our maintenance contractor, RailWorks Infrastructure, will be in attendance. Staff will be available to explain the scope of the works, the planned timetable changes, and the measures in place to manage noise, dust, and traffic during the construction period.

**What will be covered**

The session will cover the following topics:

- Overview of the track and signalling renewal works at Eaglehawk Junction
- The planned closure of the line between Bendigo and Eaglehawk from Saturday 3 August to Sunday 11 August 2024
- Replacement bus services and other travel options during the closure
- Construction hours, access points, and expected heavy vehicle movements
- Safety measures around the rail corridor
- How residents and businesses can stay informed as the works progress

There will be time for open questions at the end of the presentation. If you are unable to attend but would like to raise a concern or ask a question, you can submit it in writing using the contact details below. Written questions received by Wednesday 24 July 2024 will be collated and answered at the session, with responses published on the VRRA website afterwards.

**How to RSVP**

Please RSVP by Tuesday 23 July 2024 so that we can confirm numbers for catering and seating. You can RSVP in any of the following ways:

- Email: community@vrra.vic.gov.au (please include “Eaglehawk community session” in the subject line)
- Phone: 1800 800 007 (toll free), between 07:00 and 21:00 AEST, seven days a week
- Online: www.vrra.vic.gov.au/eaglehawk-community-session

If you have specific accessibility requirements, such as hearing loop or wheelchair access, please let us know when you RSVP so that we can make appropriate arrangements. The venue is wheelchair accessible.

**About the works**

The maintenance works at Eaglehawk Junction are part of VRRA’s ongoing programme to renew ageing track infrastructure and improve reliability on the Bendigo-East Line. The works will include replacement of worn rail and sleepers, resurfacing of the track, and upgrades to signalling equipment at the junction.

To carry out these works safely, the line will be closed to all rail traffic between Bendigo and Eaglehawk for the full period of the closure. During this time, passenger services on the Bendigo–Eaglehawk section will be replaced by buses. Further details on replacement services are available in the public notice issued on 8 July 2024 and on the VRRA website.

**Further information**

If you have any questions about the community information session or the upcoming works, please contact VRRA customer service on 1800 800 007 (toll free) between 07:00 and 21:00 AEST, seven days a week, or email customerservice@vrra.vic.gov.au. You can also visit our website at www.vrra.vic.gov.au for the latest service updates.

VRRA looks forward to meeting with the community and answering your questions about these important maintenance works.

**VRRA Customer Service**

**Planned Track Closure: Bendigo-East Line**
**Reminder Notice – Eaglehawk Junction Maintenance Works**

VRRA wishes to remind passengers, local residents, and businesses that the planned track closure between Bendigo and Eaglehawk is now less than three weeks away. This notice repeats the key details from our earlier public notice issued on 8 July 2024 and provides a final opportunity to review the arrangements before works commence.

**Closure dates and times**

The line will be closed to all rail traffic from 21:00 on Friday 16 August 2024 through to the last service on Sunday 25 August 2024. The line will reopen for normal operations from the first service on Monday 26 August 2024.

During the closure, all trains will be replaced by buses on the Bendigo–Eaglehawk section. Passengers should allow additional travel time, as bus substitution will add approximately 15–20 minutes to the usual journey. Buses will depart from the existing bus stops at both Bendigo and Eaglehawk stations, not from the rail platforms. Please follow the signage and station staff directions.

**Speed restriction after reopening**

Following the completion of the works, a temporary speed restriction of 40 km/h will apply over the renewed section of track between Bendigo and Eaglehawk. This restriction is necessary to allow the new track to settle and will remain in place for up to four weeks after the line reopens, subject to monitoring. Trains will operate to a revised timetable during this period, and minor delays of up to five minutes may occur. These arrangements are unchanged from those described in the 8 July notice.

**What the works involve**

The maintenance works at Eaglehawk Junction will include:

- Replacement of worn rail and sleepers over approximately 1.8 km of track
- Resurfacing and ballast renewal
- Upgrades to signalling equipment at the junction
- Testing and commissioning of the new signalling system

The works are part of VRRA’s ongoing programme to renew ageing track infrastructure and improve reliability on the Bendigo-East Line.

**Community information session – reminder**

VRRA will host a community information session at the Eaglehawk Community Hall, 19 Victoria Street, Eaglehawk, on Wednesday 24 July 2024, from 18:00 to 19:30 AEST. At the session, VRRA project staff will provide an overview of the works, explain the construction methodology, and answer questions from the community.

Questions submitted by email to community@vrra.vic.gov.au by Wednesday 24 July 2024 will be collated and answered at the session, with responses published on the VRRA website afterwards.

**Access during the closure**

Local residents and businesses will retain pedestrian and vehicle access to properties throughout the works. Access across the railway line at the Eaglehawk Junction pedestrian crossing will be maintained except for short periods during major lifting operations. VRRA will provide at least 48 hours’ notice of any temporary closure of the pedestrian crossing. Emergency services access will be maintained at all times.

**Replacement bus services**

Full details of the replacement bus timetable are available on the VRRA website and at Bendigo and Eaglehawk stations. Printed copies of the bus timetable can also be obtained from the VRRA customer service centre. Passengers who require assistance boarding buses should contact VRRA customer service at least 24 hours before travel so that arrangements can be made.

**Further information**

If you have any questions about the upcoming closure or the works, please contact VRRA customer service on 1800 800 007 (toll free) between 07:00 and 21:00 AEST, seven days a week, or email customerservice@vrra.vic.gov.au. You can also visit our website at www.vrra.vic.gov.au for the latest service updates.

VRRA thanks the community for its patience while these important maintenance works are carried out.

Access to the work sites will be via the following designated routes. No unauthorised access is permitted. All access points are shown on the attached site plan (Figure 1 – Site Access Plan, drawing number BDL-MW14-SAP-001 Rev B).

**12.1 Site A – Rail Installation (Up Track, km 178.400 to km 179.200)**

- Primary access: Via the existing level crossing at Bayne Street, Eaglehawk. Turn off the Midland Highway onto Bayne Street, continue approximately 800 m to the level crossing. The site office and material storage area will be located on the northern side of the track, adjacent to the crossing, on the vacant block.
- Secondary access (emergency only): Via the maintenance access gate at the end of Old Calder Highway, approximately 1.2 km north of the primary access point. This gate will be locked and a key held by the Site A Supervisor.
- Access times: Site access for vehicles is permitted from 21:30 on 2024-08-12. No vehicle movements are permitted within the rail corridor outside of the approved possession times without prior approval from Train Control.

**12.2 Site B – Ballast Cleaning (Down Track, km 176.800 to km 177.600)**

- Primary access: Via the gravel access track off Jobson Road, approximately 2 km west of the Eaglehawk town centre. The access track runs parallel to the rail corridor for approximately 500 m. The ballast cleaner will be staged on the down track at the start of the possession.
- Secondary access: Via the pedestrian gate at the Jobson Road bridge (structure 78). This gate is for pedestrian access only.
- Access times: Site access for vehicles is permitted from 22:00 on 2024-08-12. The ballast cleaner will arrive on site under its own power, having been stabled at the Bendigo yard from 2024-08-11.

**12.3 Site C – Welding and Grinding (km 175.400 to km 175.600)**

- Primary access: Via the existing access road from the intersection of Church Street and the Calder Highway. The access road is sealed for the first 200 m, then becomes an unsealed track. This track is suitable for light vehicles and the welding truck only.
- Access times: Site access is unrestricted during the possession window. Parking is available adjacent to the access road gate.

**13. Temporary Facilities**

Temporary facilities will be provided at the following locations for the duration of the work window.

| Facility | Location | Details |
|---|---|---|
| Site office | Site A (Bayne Street, Eaglehawk) | 20 ft shipping container converted for office use. Equipped with power, lighting, heating, and a first aid kit. |
| Lunch room / amenity | Site A (Bayne Street, Eaglehawk) | 20 ft shipping container with tables, chairs, a microwave, and a kettle. Separate portable toilets will be located adjacent. |
| Portable toilets | Site A and Site B | One unit at each site. Serviced daily by a contracted supplier. |
| Water supply | Site A | Potable water supplied via a 500 L water cart, refilled as required. Water at Site B and Site C is for non-potable use only (e.g., cleaning, dust suppression). |
| Power supply | Site A | Supplied by a 20 kVA diesel generator. Generator to be refuelled by the contractor. Fuel storage to comply with EPA requirements. |
| First aid | Site A (site office) and Site B (ballast cleaner cabin) | Level 2 first aid kits. A qualified first aider will be present at each site during all work periods. |
**14. Communications and Reporting**

**14.1 General**

All personnel working under this maintenance plan shall comply with the communication protocols
set out in this section. The protocols are designed to ensure that all parties have a common
understanding of the work being undertaken, the status of the works, and any issues that arise
during the possession window. The protocols apply to all contractor personnel, VRRA staff, and any
third parties authorised to enter the work sites.

**14.2 Communication Equipment**

The following communication equipment will be in use during the possession window:

- UHF CB radios (channels as per the site induction pack) for all site-to-site and site-to-control
  communications. Channel 5 will be the primary working channel. Channel 3 will be used as a
  secondary channel for logistics and non-safety communications.
- Mobile phones for all supervisory staff. A list of contact numbers will be provided in the site
  induction pack and posted in the site office at Site A.
- A dedicated landline telephone at the Site A site office for communications with the VRRA
  Network Control Centre (NCC) and emergency services. The number is listed in the emergency
  contact section of this plan.
- Satellite phone (held by the Works Supervisor) for use in the event of mobile network failure.
  The satellite phone will be tested at the start of each shift.

All communication equipment will be checked at the start of each shift. Any faults are to be
reported immediately to the Works Supervisor, who will arrange for replacement equipment.

**14.3 Communication Protocols**

The following protocols apply during the possession window:

- All personnel working on or near the track shall carry a UHF CB radio or mobile phone at all
  times. Personnel working alone shall carry a personal distress beacon (PDB) in addition to a
  radio.
- The Works Supervisor shall conduct a radio check with the Site Supervisors at the start of each
  shift and at 13:00 each day.
- Site Supervisors shall report the following to the Works Supervisor:
  - Start of work at each site;
  - Completion of any major work activity (e.g., ballast cleaning at Site B, welding at Site C);
  - Any safety incidents or near misses;
  - Any delays to the programme;
  - Any requests for additional resources or materials.
- The Works Supervisor shall report the following to the VRRA Project Manager and the NCC:
  - Confirmation of possession start and end;
  - Any safety incidents or near misses;
  - Any deviations from the approved work plan;
  - Any requests for extension of the possession window;
  - Any issues that may affect the safe operation of the line after the possession is released.
- All radio communications shall use the phonetic alphabet for spelling out location names and
  other critical information. For example, Site B shall be referred to as "Site Bravo" and Site C
  as "Site Charlie".
- All communications shall be clear, concise, and professional. Swearing and unnecessary chatter
  on the working channel are prohibited.

**14.4 Daily Reporting**

A daily progress report will be prepared by the Works Supervisor and submitted to the VRRA Project
Manager by 18:00 each day of the possession. The report will include:

- Summary of work completed that day, by site;
- Summary of work planned for the following day;
- Any safety incidents or near misses (full details to be provided separately);
- Any issues or concerns, including weather-related delays, equipment faults, or material
  shortages;
- Confirmation that all personnel are accounted for at the end of the shift.

The daily report will be submitted by email to the VRRA Project Manager. A hard copy will be filed
in the site office.

**14.5 Reporting Lines**

The reporting lines for the possession window are as follows:

- All contractor personnel report to their respective Site Supervisor.
- Site Supervisors report to the Works Supervisor.
- The Works Supervisor reports to the VRRA Project Manager for all matters relating to the scope,
  programme, and quality of the works.
- For all matters relating to track safety, possession management, and signalling, the Works
  Supervisor reports directly to the VRRA Network Control Centre (NCC).
- The VRRA Project Manager is the primary point of contact for the contractor for all commercial
  and contractual matters.
**15. Quality Assurance and Inspection**

Quality assurance for the works under Window MW14 will be delivered through a combination of
pre-start inspections, in-process checks, and post-completion verification. The contractor's
Quality Manager, in consultation with the VRRA Project Manager, will maintain a site-specific
Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) covering all activities listed in Section 5 of this plan. The
ITP will identify hold points and witness points for each activity, and no work shall proceed
past a hold point without the required inspection and written endorsement.

**15.1 Pre-Start Inspections**

Prior to the commencement of any works at each site on the first day of the possession, the
following inspections shall be completed and recorded:

- Visual inspection of all plant and equipment for serviceability, including hydraulic systems,
  lifting attachments, and emergency stop functions;
- Calibration check of all survey and measuring equipment, with certificates available for
  review;
- Inspection of all temporary works, including fencing, signage, and lighting, against the
  approved Traffic Management Plan;
- Confirmation that all materials delivered to site match the approved material schedule,
  including batch numbers for any ballast or geotextile;
- Toolbox talk attendance records, confirming that all personnel have received the site-specific
  induction and are aware of the day's activities and exclusion zones.

Pre-start inspection records will be kept in the site office and made available to VRRA
representatives on request. Any non-conformance identified during pre-start inspection shall be
rectified before the affected activity commences.

**15.2 In-Process Inspection Checkpoints**

The following inspection checkpoints will apply during the works. These are in addition to the
hold points and witness points listed in the ITP.

| Checkpoint | Location | Timing | Responsible | Verification |
|------------|----------|--------|-------------|--------------|
| ICP-01 | Site A – excavation line | After first 50 m of excavation | Works Supervisor | Check depth, width, and alignment against design drawings; record any unexpected services |
| ICP-02 | Site B – drainage installation | Every 20th pipe joint | Site Supervisor (B) | Confirm joint alignment and bedding compaction; photograph each joint |
| ICP-03 | Site B – backfill lift | Each 300 mm lift | Site Supervisor (B) | Confirm compaction test results are within specification |
| ICP-04 | Site C – rail grinding | Start of each grinding pass | Site Supervisor (C) | Confirm grinding pattern and depth of cut against approved parameters |
| ICP-05 | Site C – rail surface | After final pass | Quality Manager | Verify surface finish, absence of burns, and profile against template |
| ICP-06 | All sites – housekeeping | End of each shift | Works Supervisor | Confirm tools, plant, and materials are secured; walkway clear |
| ICP-07 | All sites – environmental | Daily, mid-shift | Environmental Representative | Check sediment controls, spill kits, and noise monitoring compliance |

Inspection results will be recorded on the standard VRRA inspection form (VRRA-QA-014) and
retained in the site office. Any non-conformance raised during in-process inspection will be
logged on the Non-Conformance Register and actioned in accordance with Section 15.4.

**15.3 Survey and Geometry Verification**

The contractor shall engage a licensed surveyor to verify track geometry after the completion of
works at each site. The survey shall be carried out prior to the release of the possession and
shall confirm:

- Track gauge within ±3 mm of nominal;
- Cant within ±5 mm of design;
- Vertical alignment within ±5 mm over any 10 m chord;
- Horizontal alignment within ±5 mm over any 10 m chord;
- Clearance to adjacent structures within the limits shown on the design drawings.

Survey results will be provided to the VRRA Project Manager in a written report, including a
plan showing the surveyed positions and any deviations. Where deviations are outside the limits
above, the contractor shall propose rectification works for approval prior to the release of the
possession.

Archive item 3: Engineering Assessment: Eaglehawk Road Bridge
Source format: Engineering Assessment

| Attribute | Detail |
| --- | --- |
| Asset number | VRRA-BDG-2214 |
| Bridge type | Two-span steel girder, concrete deck |
| Span arrangement | 2 x 14.6 m |
| Overall length | 29.2 m |
| Deck width | 11.0 m (kerb to kerb) |
| Carriageway width | 9.4 m (two lanes) |
| Skew | 12 degrees |
| Bearings | Elastomeric bearing pads (4 per span, 8 total) |
| Deck waterproofing | Torch-on membrane, installed 2011 |
| Abutments | Reinforced concrete, shallow spread footings |
| Piers | Single reinforced concrete column with headstock |
| Annual average daily traffic | 4,800 vehicles (2023 count) |
| Rail clearance | 5.6 m above rail level (minimum, at mid-span) |

2.2 Site Context

The bridge is located in an urban residential area of Eaglehawk, with the nearest adjacent property being the Eaglehawk Primary School, approximately 90 m to the north-east. The rail corridor beneath the bridge carries both freight services (grain and container traffic) and the Bendigo – Swan Hill passenger service, which operates four return services per day. The nearest level crossing is at Victoria Street, approximately 400 m to the south.

The bridge is a key access route for local residents and is also used by school buses and emergency services vehicles. There are no current load restrictions on the bridge, however the posted speed limit on the bridge is 60 km/h.

3. Inspection Details

3.1 Inspection Dates

The bridge was inspected on 19 March 2024. The inspection was carried out under clear weather conditions with an ambient temperature of 18°C. Access was provided by an underbridge inspection unit for the soffit, bearings, and pier, and by foot for the deck and parapets. A secondary inspection of the waterproofing membrane and bearing condition was undertaken on 2 April 2024 following a period of heavy rainfall, to assess water ingress paths.

3.2 Inspection Personnel

- Lead Inspector: M. Okafor, Senior Structures Engineer
- Assistant Inspector: J. Wright, Structures Technician
- Traffic Control: Bendigo Traffic Services (permit no. TCS-2024-0311)

3.3 Previous Inspection History

Eaglehawk Road Bridge required repair scope is replacement of bearing pads and waterproofing membrane. Record status: current.

Table 2: Previous inspection summary

| Inspection date | Assessment ref | Overall condition | Key findings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 15 June 2020 | EA-2020-055 | Good | Minor cracking in deck soffit; no action required |
| 12 June 2023 | EA-2023-089 | Fair | Water staining at bearing locations; bearing pads showing surface cracking; waterproofing membrane showing areas of blistering |
| 19 March 2024 | EA-2024-114 (this report) | Fair to Poor | Deterioration of bearing pads and waterproofing membrane has progressed; repair scope confirmed |

Note: The 2020 assessment identified no structural concerns. The 2023 assessment recommended monitoring of the bearing pads and waterproofing membrane, with a follow-up inspection within 12 months. This assessment fulfils that requirement.

4. Condition Assessment

4.1 Deck and Wearing Surface

The concrete deck was visually inspected from the underside using the underbridge unit and from above following removal of a small section of the wearing course at the southern edge of the deck. The wearing surface (asphalt, 40 mm nominal) shows general cracking consistent with age, but no significant potholes or deformation. The deck soffit shows hairline longitudinal cracking over the pier headstock, consistent with the 2020 inspection. Crack widths are less than 0.2 mm and no active rust staining was observed at the cracks.

The deck surface was core sampled at two locations (cores D-1 and D-2, taken 19 March 2024). Both cores showed the asphalt wearing course to be sound, with no evidence of moisture trapped at the interface between asphalt and waterproofing membrane.

Condition rating: 2 (Fair) – no immediate structural concern.

4.2 Waterproofing Membrane

The waterproofing membrane was installed in 2011 as part of a deck rehabilitation. The membrane is a torch-on polymer modified bitumen membrane, 3 mm thick, with a protective geotextile layer. The membrane was inspected from the underside of the deck where it is visible at the deck edges, and from above at the two core locations.
**VRRA Engineering Assessment – EA-2024-114 (continued)**

**4.3 Bearings and Bearing Pads**

The bridge carries the Eaglehawk Road alignment over the Bendigo–Echuca rail corridor at approximate chainage 158.240 km on the Bendigo Corridor. The structure is a three-span continuous concrete slab bridge, span arrangement 11.0 m – 16.5 m – 11.0 m, supported on elastomeric bearing pads at the abutments and on the two intermediate piers. The bearings were last replaced in 2011 as part of the deck rehabilitation works.

Inspection of the bearing pads from the underbridge unit at both abutments and both pier headstocks confirmed the following:

- Abutment A1: The west bearing pad shows surface cracking across approximately 60% of the pad area. Cracks are longitudinal and up to 2 mm wide at the surface. No extrusion or delamination was observed. The east pad shows lighter cracking, limited to the outer 20 mm of the pad edge. Both pads remain seated correctly with no evidence of slip.
- Pier P1: The north bearing pad shows moderate surface cracking and slight bulging along the front face. The south pad shows similar cracking but no bulging. Minor water staining was observed on the headstock directly beneath the north pad, consistent with the staining noted in the 2023 assessment.
- Pier P2: Both bearing pads show surface cracking similar to that at Pier P1. In addition, the east pad shows a 30 mm length of edge spalling on the elastomer at the outer corner. The spalling is shallow (less than 5 mm) and does not expose any internal shims.
- Abutment A2: Bearing pads show surface cracking consistent with Abutment A1, but no bulging or spalling was observed.

The cracking pattern observed is consistent with age-related surface degradation of the elastomer. The 2023 assessment noted surface cracking and recommended monitoring. The progression since 2023 is moderate: crack widths have increased by approximately 0.5 mm at the most affected locations, and the bulging at Pier P1 north pad is new since the 2023 inspection. The edge spalling at Pier P2 east pad is also new.

Bearing pad hardness was spot-checked using a Shore A durometer at accessible locations. Readings ranged from 58 to 64, compared with a typical new pad hardness of 60 ± 5. The readings are within the expected range for pads of this age and do not indicate significant loss of elasticity.

Condition rating: 3 (Poor) – deterioration is progressing and repair is recommended within 12 months.

**4.4 Substructure (Abutments and Piers)**

The abutments and piers are reinforced concrete with a painted finish. The paint system is showing general weathering, with localised areas of bubbling and flaking at the abutment wingwalls. No active rust staining, spalling, or delamination was observed on the structural faces.

At Pier P1, the headstock shows a vertical hairline crack on the north face, approximately 0.15 mm wide, extending from the bearing shelf downward for approximately 400 mm. The crack was noted in the 2023 assessment and has not propagated. Crack monitoring was not installed; the lack of propagation over 12 months suggests the crack is non-structural and likely shrinkage-related.

The abutment ballast walls show minor efflorescence at the base, consistent with seasonal moisture. No loss of section was observed.

Condition rating: 2 (Fair) – no immediate action required beyond routine maintenance.

**4.5 Rail Corridor Interface**

The bridge crosses the rail corridor at a skew of approximately 15 degrees. The minimum vertical clearance from rail level to the underside of the bridge superstructure was measured at 5.85 m at the lowest point, which exceeds the minimum clearance of 5.60 m specified in the VRRA Engineering Standard for this corridor classification. The clearance was measured using the laser rangefinder from the rail level at three locations across the track width; the minimum recorded value is reported above.

The bridge drainage outlets on the southern side discharge directly adjacent to the ballast shoulder. During the inspection, no active discharge was observed, but staining on the ballast suggests intermittent discharge during rain events. This is a maintenance issue rather than a structural concern, but it should be addressed as part of the recommended drainage works.

**Planned Track Closure: Bendigo-East Line**

**Victorian Regional Rail Authority (VRRA) – Public Notice**

**Issued:** Monday, 10 June 2024

**Effective dates:** Monday, 12 August 2024 to Friday, 16 August 2024 (inclusive)

**Line:** Bendigo-East Line (Bendigo to Eaglehawk section)

The Victorian Regional Rail Authority (VRRA) advises passengers and members of the community that scheduled maintenance works will be undertaken on the Bendigo-East Line between Bendigo and Eaglehawk. The Bendigo-East Line scheduled maintenance closure dates are 2024-08-12 to 2024-08-16. Record status: superseded.

During this period, the line will be closed to all train traffic to allow crews to carry out essential track resurfacing, drainage improvements, and the replacement of worn sleepers and fastenings in the Eaglehawk Road corridor. These works are part of VRRA’s ongoing commitment to maintaining a safe and reliable regional rail network.

**What this means for passengers**

Train services on the Bendigo-East Line will not operate between Bendigo and Eaglehawk during the closure period. Passengers are advised to plan alternative travel arrangements. A dedicated replacement coach service will operate between Bendigo and Eaglehawk, stopping at all regular stations on the line.

Replacement coaches will depart Bendigo and Eaglehawk at the usual scheduled train times. Please note that coach journey times may be longer than normal train travel times due to road traffic conditions and the need to stop at all stations. Passengers should allow extra time for their journey.

Passengers travelling beyond Eaglehawk, including those connecting to services on the wider regional network, should check the VRRA website or the Journey Planner for updated connection times.

**Access and safety**

For the safety of passengers, staff, and contractors, the track and station platforms within the work zone will be closed to the public for the duration of the works. Please observe all signage and follow the directions of VRRA staff and authorised contractors on site.

Residents and businesses in the vicinity of the works may notice increased activity, including the presence of heavy machinery, temporary lighting, and noise from construction equipment during daylight hours. Works will be carried out between 06:00 and 18:00 AEST on each day of the closure, weather permitting.

**Alternative travel information**

- Replacement coaches will operate between Bendigo and Eaglehawk for the full duration of the closure.
- For passengers requiring accessible transport, please contact VRRA customer service at least 24 hours in advance to arrange assistance.
- Local bus services operated by the City of Greater Bendigo will continue to run their normal routes and may provide an alternative option for some journeys.
- Cyclists and pedestrians are advised that the shared path adjacent to the rail corridor between Bendigo and Eaglehawk will remain open, except where temporary fencing is required for safety. Please follow any detour signage in place.

**Further information**

VRRA thanks passengers and the community for their patience while these important maintenance works are carried out. We understand that track closures can be inconvenient, and we appreciate your understanding as we work to improve the reliability of the line.

For the latest service information, please visit the VRRA website at www.vrra.vic.gov.au or check the Journey Planner before you travel. You can also follow VRRA on social media for real-time updates.

For customer service enquiries, contact VRRA on 1800 800 007 (toll free) between 07:00 and 21:00 AEST, seven days a week. Hearing or speech impaired customers can contact us via the National Relay Service on 133 677.

**About these works**

The scheduled maintenance closure of the Bendigo-East Line has been planned to minimise disruption to passengers and the community. Works of this nature require the line to be closed to train traffic to ensure the safety of workers and the integrity of the track. VRRA will continue to advise the community of any future planned closures as part of our regular maintenance programme.

**Speed Restriction Advisory – Eaglehawk Junction**

VRRA advises passengers and the local community that, in addition to the planned track closure detailed in our previous notice, a temporary speed restriction will be in place at Eaglehawk Junction for the duration of the maintenance works.

**Location of speed restriction**

The temporary speed restriction applies to the section of track at Eaglehawk Junction, located approximately 6 kilometres west of Bendigo station. The restriction covers the junction area where the line to Eaglehawk station diverges from the main Bendigo-East Line, including the points and crossing loops in that vicinity. Trains travelling through this section, in either direction, will be subject to the reduced speed limit for the entire period of the closure.

**Speed limit and timing**

Eaglehawk Junction temporary speed restriction is 40 km/h. Record status: superseded. This speed limit will be in force from the commencement of the closure at 06:00 AEST on Saturday 16 November 2024 until the cessation of works at 18:00 AEST on Sunday 24 November 2024. The 40 km/h restriction will apply continuously throughout the closure period, including at times when no works are actively being undertaken on the track, as the condition of the track bed and the presence of temporary infrastructure require a reduced speed for safe passage.

**Reason for the restriction**

The speed restriction has been implemented for the following reasons:

- The replacement of timber sleepers and resurfacing of the track bed in the junction area leaves the track in a condition that is not suitable for normal line speeds until it has been stabilised and tamped.
- Temporary track alignment adjustments are required to accommodate the works, and these adjustments are only certified for transit at reduced speed.
- The presence of construction plant and personnel working in close proximity to the running line necessitates a lower speed to ensure the safety of all workers and passengers.

The restriction is a standard safety measure for works of this nature and will be lifted once the track has been inspected, certified, and returned to a condition suitable for normal operating speeds. VRRA will issue a further notice advising when the restriction has been removed.

**What this means for passengers**

While the speed restriction is in place, train services will not operate through the affected section, as the line will be closed to all rail traffic for the duration of the works. The speed restriction will apply to any maintenance vehicles, engineering trains, or other rail traffic that may be required to move through the junction area during the works. Passenger services will resume at normal line speeds once the restriction has been lifted and the track has been certified safe for operation.

**Safety advice for the community**

Residents and businesses in the vicinity of Eaglehawk Junction are reminded to exercise caution near the rail corridor during the works period. The following safety advice applies:

- Do not enter the rail corridor at any time. The corridor is private property and access is strictly prohibited.
- Be aware of increased heavy vehicle movements on local roads, including access roads to the worksite. Please take care when driving or walking near these areas.
- Temporary fencing and signage will be in place to direct pedestrians and vehicles away from work areas. Please follow all directions and do not remove or interfere with fencing.
- Parents are encouraged to remind children of the dangers of playing near railway tracks and to keep clear of the corridor at all times.
- If you observe any unauthorised access to the rail corridor, please report it to VRRA on the customer service number below or to Victoria Police.

**Enquiries and further information**

For further information about this speed restriction or the planned track closure, please contact VRRA customer service on 1800 800 007 (toll free) between 07:00 and 21:00 AEST, seven days a week. You can also email us at customerservice@vrra.vic.gov.au or visit our website at www.vrra.vic.gov.au for the latest service updates.

VRRA thanks the community for its patience and understanding while these important maintenance works are carried out. We will continue to provide updates as the works progress.

**Planned Track Closure: Bendigo-East Line**
**Reminder Notice – Eaglehawk Junction Maintenance Works**

VRRA wishes to remind passengers, local residents, and businesses that the planned track closure between Bendigo and Eaglehawk is now less than three weeks away. This notice repeats the key details from our earlier public notice issued on 8 July 2024 and provides a final opportunity to review the arrangements before works commence.

**Closure dates and times**

The line will be closed to all rail traffic from 21:00 on Friday 16 August 2024 through to the last service on Sunday 25 August 2024. The line will reopen for normal operations from the first service on Monday 26 August 2024.

During the closure, all trains will be replaced by buses on the Bendigo–Eaglehawk section. Passengers should allow additional travel time, as bus substitution will add approximately 15–20 minutes to the usual journey. Buses will depart from the existing bus stops at both Bendigo and Eaglehawk stations, not from the rail platforms. Please follow the signage and station staff directions.

**Speed restriction after reopening**

Following the completion of the works, a temporary speed restriction of 40 km/h will apply over the renewed section of track between Bendigo and Eaglehawk. This restriction is necessary to allow the new track to settle and will remain in place for up to four weeks after the line reopens, subject to monitoring. Trains will operate to a revised timetable during this period, and minor delays of up to five minutes may occur. These arrangements are unchanged from those described in the 8 July notice.

**What the works involve**

The maintenance works at Eaglehawk Junction will include:

- Replacement of worn rail and sleepers over approximately 1.8 km of track
- Resurfacing and ballast renewal
- Upgrades to signalling equipment at the junction

**14. Communications and Reporting**

**14.1 General**

All personnel working under this maintenance plan shall comply with the communication protocols
set out in this section. The protocols are designed to ensure that all parties have a common
understanding of the work being undertaken, the status of the works, and any issues that arise
during the possession window. The protocols apply to all contractor personnel, VRRA staff, and any
third parties authorised to enter the work sites.

**14.2 Communication Equipment**

The following communication equipment will be in use during the possession window:

- UHF CB radios (channels as per the site induction pack) for all site-to-site and site-to-control
  communications. Channel 5 will be the primary working channel. Channel 3 will be used as a
  secondary channel for logistics and non-safety communications.
- Mobile phones for all supervisory staff. A list of contact numbers will be provided in the site
  induction pack and posted in the site office at Site A.
- A dedicated landline telephone at the Site A site office for communications with the VRRA
  Network Control Centre (NCC) and emergency services. The number is listed in the emergency
  contact section of this plan.
- Satellite phone (held by the Works Supervisor) for use in the event of mobile network failure.
  The satellite phone will be tested at the start of each shift.

All communication equipment will be checked at the start of each shift. Any faults are to be
reported immediately to the Works Supervisor, who will arrange for replacement equipment.

**14.3 Communication Protocols**

The following protocols apply during the possession window:

- All personnel working on or near the track shall carry a UHF CB radio or mobile phone at all
  times. Personnel working alone shall carry a personal distress beacon (PDB) in addition to a
  radio.
- The Works Supervisor shall conduct a radio check with the Site Supervisors at the start of each
  shift and at 13:00 each day.
- Site Supervisors shall report the following to the Works Supervisor:
  - Start of work at each site;
  - Completion of any major work activity (e.g., ballast cleaning at Site B, welding at Site C);
  - Any safety incidents or near misses;
  - Any delays to the programme;
  - Any requests for additional resources or materials.
- The Works Supervisor shall report the following to the VRRA Project Manager and the NCC:
  - Confirmation of possession start and end;
  - Any safety incidents or near misses;
  - Any deviations from the approved work plan;
  - Any requests for extension of the possession window;
  - Any issues that may affect the safe operation of the line after the possession is released.
- All radio communications shall use the phonetic alphabet for spelling out location names and
  other critical information. For example, Site B shall be referred to as "Site Bravo" and Site C
  as "Site Charlie".
- All communications shall be clear, concise, and professional. Swearing and unnecessary chatter
  on the working channel are prohibited.

A daily progress report will be prepared by the Works Supervisor and submitted to the VRRA Project
Manager by 18:00 each day of the possession. The report will include:

- Summary of work completed that day, by site;
- Summary of work planned for the following day;
- Any safety incidents or near misses (full details to be provided separately);
- Any issues or concerns, including weather-related delays, equipment faults, or material
  shortages;

The daily report will be submitted by email to the VRRA Project Manager. A hard copy will be filed
in the site office.

The reporting lines for the possession window are as follows:

- The Works Supervisor reports to the VRRA Project Manager for all matters relating to the scope,

  Supervisor reports directly to the VRRA Network Control Centre (NCC).

  and contractual matters.

**15. Quality Assurance and Inspection**

Quality assurance for the works under Window MW14 will be delivered through a combination of
pre-start inspections, in-process checks, and post-completion verification. The contractor's
Quality Manager, in consultation with the VRRA Project Manager, will maintain a site-specific
Inspection and Test Plan (ITP) covering all activities listed in Section 5 of this plan. The
ITP will identify hold points and witness points for each activity, and no work shall proceed
past a hold point without the required inspection and written endorsement.

**15.1 Pre-Start Inspections**

Prior to the commencement of any works at each site on the first day of the possession, the
following inspections shall be completed and recorded:

- Visual inspection of all plant and equipment for serviceability, including hydraulic systems,
  lifting attachments, and emergency stop functions;
- Calibration check of all survey and measuring equipment, with certificates available for
  review;
- Inspection of all temporary works, including fencing, signage, and lighting, against the
  approved Traffic Management Plan;
- Confirmation that all materials delivered to site match the approved material schedule,
  including batch numbers for any ballast or geotextile;
- Toolbox talk attendance records, confirming that all personnel have received the site-specific
  induction and are aware of the day's activities and exclusion zones.

Pre-start inspection records will be kept in the site office and made available to VRRA
representatives on request. Any non-conformance identified during pre-start inspection shall be
rectified before the affected activity commences.

**15.2 In-Process Inspection Checkpoints**

The following inspection checkpoints will apply during the works. These are in addition to the
hold points and witness points listed in the ITP.

| Checkpoint | Location | Timing | Responsible | Verification |
|------------|----------|--------|-------------|--------------|
| ICP-01 | Site A – excavation line | After first 50 m of excavation | Works Supervisor | Check depth, width, and alignment against design drawings; record any unexpected services |
| ICP-02 | Site B – drainage installation | Every 20th pipe joint | Site Supervisor (B) | Confirm joint alignment and bedding compaction; photograph each joint |
| ICP-03 | Site B – backfill lift | Each 300 mm lift | Site Supervisor (B) | Confirm compaction test results are within specification |
| ICP-04 | Site C – rail grinding | Start of each grinding pass | Site Supervisor (C) | Confirm grinding pattern and depth of cut against approved parameters |
| ICP-05 | Site C – rail surface | After final pass | Quality Manager | Verify surface finish, absence of burns, and profile against template |
| ICP-06 | All sites – housekeeping | End of each shift | Works Supervisor | Confirm tools, plant, and materials are secured; walkway clear |
| ICP-07 | All sites – environmental | Daily, mid-shift | Environmental Representative | Check sediment controls, spill kits, and noise monitoring compliance |

Inspection results will be recorded on the standard VRRA inspection form (VRRA-QA-014) and
retained in the site office. Any non-conformance raised during in-process inspection will be
logged on the Non-Conformance Register and actioned in accordance with Section 15.4.

**15.3 Survey and Geometry Verification**

The contractor shall engage a licensed surveyor to verify track geometry after the completion of
works at each site. The survey shall be carried out prior to the release of the possession and
shall confirm:

- Track gauge within ±3 mm of nominal;
- Cant within ±5 mm of design;
- Vertical alignment within ±5 mm over any 10 m chord;
- Horizontal alignment within ±5 mm over any 10 m chord;
- Clearance to adjacent structures within the limits shown on the design drawings.

Survey results will be provided to the VRRA Project Manager in a written report, including a
plan showing the surveyed positions and any deviations. Where deviations are outside the limits
above, the contractor shall propose rectification works for approval prior to the release of the
possession.

2.2 Site Context

The bridge is located in an urban residential area of Eaglehawk, with the nearest adjacent property being the Eaglehawk Primary School, approximately 90 m to the north-east. The rail corridor beneath the bridge carries both freight services (grain and container traffic) and the Bendigo – Swan Hill passenger service, which operates four return services per day. The nearest level crossing is at Victoria Street, approximately 400 m to the south.

The bridge is a key access route for local residents and is also used by school buses and emergency services vehicles. There are no current load restrictions on the bridge, however the posted speed limit on the bridge is 60 km/h.

3. Inspection Details

3.1 Inspection Dates

The bridge was inspected on 19 March 2024. The inspection was carried out under clear weather conditions with an ambient temperature of 18°C. Access was provided by an underbridge inspection unit for the soffit, bearings, and pier, and by foot for the deck and parapets. A secondary inspection of the waterproofing membrane and bearing condition was undertaken on 2 April 2024 following a period of heavy rainfall, to assess water ingress paths.

3.2 Inspection Personnel

- Lead Inspector: M. Okafor, Senior Structures Engineer
- Assistant Inspector: J. Wright, Structures Technician
- Traffic Control: Bendigo Traffic Services (permit no. TCS-2024-0311)

3.3 Previous Inspection History

Eaglehawk Road Bridge required repair scope is replacement of bearing pads and waterproofing membrane. Record status: current.

Table 2: Previous inspection summary

| Inspection date | Assessment ref | Overall condition | Key findings |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 15 June 2020 | EA-2020-055 | Good | Minor cracking in deck soffit; no action required |
| 12 June 2023 | EA-2023-089 | Fair | Water staining at bearing locations; bearing pads showing surface cracking; waterproofing membrane showing areas of blistering |
| 19 March 2024 | EA-2024-114 (this report) | Fair to Poor | Deterioration of bearing pads and waterproofing membrane has progressed; repair scope confirmed |

Note: The 2020 assessment identified no structural concerns. The 2023 assessment recommended monitoring of the bearing pads and waterproofing membrane, with a follow-up inspection within 12 months. This assessment fulfils that requirement.

4. Condition Assessment

4.1 Deck and Wearing Surface

The concrete deck was visually inspected from the underside using the underbridge unit and from above following removal of a small section of the wearing course at the southern edge of the deck. The wearing surface (asphalt, 40 mm nominal) shows general cracking consistent with age, but no significant potholes or deformation. The deck soffit shows hairline longitudinal cracking over the pier headstock, consistent with the 2020 inspection. Crack widths are less than 0.2 mm and no active rust staining was observed at the cracks.

The deck surface was core sampled at two locations (cores D-1 and D-2, taken 19 March 2024). Both cores showed the asphalt wearing course to be sound, with no evidence of moisture trapped at the interface between asphalt and waterproofing membrane.

Condition rating: 2 (Fair) – no immediate structural concern.

4.2 Waterproofing Membrane

The waterproofing membrane was installed in 2011 as part of a deck rehabilitation. The membrane is a torch-on polymer modified bitumen membrane, 3 mm thick, with a protective geotextile layer. The membrane was inspected from the underside of the deck where it is visible at the deck edges, and from above at the two core locations.

documents.title: Engineering Assessment: Eaglehawk Road Bridge
documents.content:
**VRRA Engineering Assessment – EA-2024-114 (continued)**

**4.3 Bearings and Bearing Pads**

The bridge carries the Eaglehawk Road alignment over the Bendigo–Echuca rail corridor at approximate chainage 158.240 km on the Bendigo Corridor. The structure is a three-span continuous concrete slab bridge, span arrangement 11.0 m – 16.5 m – 11.0 m, supported on elastomeric bearing pads at the abutments and on the two intermediate piers. The bearings were last replaced in 2011 as part of the deck rehabilitation works.

Inspection of the bearing pads from the underbridge unit at both abutments and both pier headstocks confirmed the following:

- Abutment A1: The west bearing pad shows surface cracking across approximately 60% of the pad area. Cracks are longitudinal and up to 2 mm wide at the surface. No extrusion or delamination was observed. The east pad shows lighter cracking, limited to the outer 20 mm of the pad edge. Both pads remain seated correctly with no evidence of slip.
- Pier P1: The north bearing pad shows moderate surface cracking and slight bulging along the front face. The south pad shows similar cracking but no bulging. Minor water staining was observed on the headstock directly beneath the north pad, consistent with the staining noted in the 2023 assessment.
- Pier P2: Both bearing pads show surface cracking similar to that at Pier P1. In addition, the east pad shows a 30 mm length of edge spalling on the elastomer at the outer corner. The spalling is shallow (less than 5 mm) and does not expose any internal shims.
- Abutment A2: Bearing pads show surface cracking consistent with Abutment A1, but no bulging or spalling was observed.

The cracking pattern observed is consistent with age-related surface degradation of the elastomer. The 2023 assessment noted surface cracking and recommended monitoring. The progression since 2023 is moderate: crack widths have increased by approximately 0.5 mm at the most affected locations, and the bulging at Pier P1 north pad is new since the 2023 inspection. The edge spalling at Pier P2 east pad is also new.

Bearing pad hardness was spot-checked using a Shore A durometer at accessible locations. Readings ranged from 58 to 64, compared with a typical new pad hardness of 60 ± 5. The readings are within the expected range for pads of this age and do not indicate significant loss of elasticity.

Condition rating: 3 (Poor) – deterioration is progressing and repair is recommended within 12 months.

**4.4 Substructure (Abutments and Piers)**

The abutments and piers are reinforced concrete with a painted finish. The paint system is showing general weathering, with localised areas of bubbling and flaking at the abutment wingwalls. No active rust staining, spalling, or delamination was observed on the structural faces.

At Pier P1, the headstock shows a vertical hairline crack on the north face, approximately 0.15 mm wide, extending from the bearing shelf downward for approximately 400 mm. The crack was noted in the 2023 assessment and has not propagated. Crack monitoring was not installed; the lack of propagation over 12 months suggests the crack is non-structural and likely shrinkage-related.

The abutment ballast walls show minor efflorescence at the base, consistent with seasonal moisture. No loss of section was observed.

Condition rating: 2 (Fair) – no immediate action required beyond routine maintenance.

**4.5 Rail Corridor Interface**

The bridge crosses the rail corridor at a skew of approximately 15 degrees. The minimum vertical clearance from rail level to the underside of the bridge superstructure was measured at 5.85 m at the lowest point, which exceeds the minimum clearance of 5.60 m specified in the VRRA Engineering Standard for this corridor classification. The clearance was measured using the laser rangefinder from the rail level at three locations across the track width; the minimum recorded value is reported above.

The bridge drainage outlets on the southern side discharge directly adjacent to the ballast shoulder. During the inspection, no active discharge was observed, but staining on the ballast suggests intermittent discharge during rain events. This is a maintenance issue rather than a structural concern, but it should be addressed as part of the recommended drainage works.
